bull.b: WTW converts a high share of reported earnings into cash: TTM FCF of ~$1.63B (~87% of net income). This durable cash conversion from fee and recurring outsourcing revenues supports buybacks, dividends, reinvestment and balance-sheet resilience over the next 2–6 months.

Management has a clear, time‑bound margin plan targeting ~100 bps annual adjusted operating margin expansion, supported by AI, automation and Neuron rollouts. These structural productivity initiatives can sustainably lift profitability and operating leverage across cycles.

Health and broader HWC show recurring, inflation‑linked demand (Health +6%) and high margins (27.3%), providing steady fee revenue and margin stability. This segment’s recurring nature and favorable secular trends support predictable medium‑term cash and profit fundamentals.

bear.b: Leverage has increased materially versus prior years (TTM D/E ~0.87), reducing financial flexibility if revenue or margins deteriorate. Higher absolute debt raises interest and refinancing exposure and constrains capital deployment options during downturns over the next several quarters.

WTW’s P&L has shown meaningful year‑to‑year swings (2024 net loss), indicating sensitivity to non‑recurring items, reserve changes or timing of large mandates. That volatility reduces predictability of cash flow and complicates benchmarking of sustainable margins over 2–6 months.

Risk & Broking slowed markedly with missed new business and narrowed guidance, while management cites heightened competitive pricing. Given R&B’s revenue weight, continued softening or price compression would structurally limit medium‑term revenue and margin upside across the business.
